metaTitle: BMW M-Power Engine Rebuild | BMW Garage
metaDescription: Specialist BMW M-Power engine rebuilds for S54, S55, S58, S62, S63, S65, S85, S68 engines. Full strip-down, precision assembly, and testing at our Essex workshop.
lede: Specialist rebuilds for BMW M-division engines — S54, S55, S58, S62, S63, S65, S85, S68. Full strip-down, precision assembly, and comprehensive testing.

blocks.html: M-Power engine rebuilding is the specialist process of rebuilding BMW's high-performance M-division engines. These S-code engines are built to tighter tolerances, produce significantly more power, and incorporate advanced systems not found on standard BMW engines. Every M-Power rebuild at our workshop follows a documented, repeatable process designed to restore the engine to its original performance specification.

We carry out M-Power rebuilds on the full range of S-code engines, including the S54 (E46 M3, Z4 M), S55 (F80 M3, F82 M4, F87 M2 Competition), S58 (G80 M3, G82 M4, G87 M2, X3 M/X4 M), S62 (E39 M5), S63 (F10 M5, F90 M5, M6, M8, X5 M/X6 M), S65 (E90/E92/E93 M3), S85 (E60 M5, E63/E64 M6), and S68 (XM, G90 M5).

paras: Prices are starting from, inclusive of full rebuild with new OEM-spec components, machining, and testing. Final quote confirmed after inspection.

blocks.html: We rebuild the full range of BMW M-Power S-code engines. Each engine has specific requirements, and our process is tailored accordingly.

For detailed information on each variant, see the relevant [M3](/bmw-m3-engines), [M4](/bmw-m4-engines), [M5](/bmw-m5-engines), [M6](/bmw-m6-engines), [M8](/bmw-m8-engines), or [M2](/bmw-m2-engines) pages.

steps.title: Strip-Down & Documentation
steps.body: Complete disassembly with careful documentation of every component's condition, orientation, and clearances.

steps.title: Component Inspection
steps.body: Every component measured against M-specification tolerances. Crankshaft assessment is critical, as M crankshafts are specific and expensive.

steps.title: Machining & Preparation
steps.body: Precision cylinder boring/honing, crankshaft grinding, and block surface preparation to exact M specifications.

steps.title: Bearing & Timing Systems
steps.body: Replacement of bearings (e.g., S54/S65/S85 rod bearings) and timing systems (chains, tensioners, VANOS).

steps.title: Precision Assembly
steps.body: Assembly using M-specification torque procedures and BMW M-specialist tooling, following TIS documentation.

steps.title: Comprehensive Testing
steps.body: Compression, pressure, and performance checks on a test stand, followed by in-vehicle road testing to verify operation.

items.q: What makes an M-Power rebuild different from a standard BMW engine rebuild?
items.a: M-Power engines (S-code) have tighter tolerances, more complex systems (individual throttle bodies, advanced VANOS), and require M-specific tooling and parts. Our rebuild process follows BMW M technical information (TIS) with specific torque and assembly procedures.

items.q: Which M-Power engines do you rebuild?
items.a: We rebuild S54, S55, S58, S62, S63, S65, S85, and S68 engines, covering the full range of M models including M2, M3, M4, M5, M6, M8, X3 M, X4 M, X5 M, X6 M, and XM.

items.q: Do you replace rod bearings on S54/S65/S85 engines?
items.a: Yes. Rod bearing replacement is a standard part of our rebuild process for these engines, as it's a known requirement to restore reliability and performance.

items.q: Do you inspect the crank hub on S55 engines?
items.a: Yes. For S55 engines (F80 M3, F82 M4, F87 M2 Competition), crank hub inspection and replacement is a standard part of our rebuild process to address the known press-fit friction design.

items.q: How long does an M-Power rebuild take?
items.a: Typical turnaround is 3-5 working days for a full rebuild, depending on the extent of the work and parts availability. This is standard across our engine rebuild services.
